h1: Fencing in Carrollton, TX: Installation, Repair and Gate Quotes
heroSub: Carrollton's 1970s to 1990s subdivisions are full of aging wood fences, alley gates and shared lines. Call now and ask for two or three comparable written quotes from independent fence contractors.
introHtml:
Fencing in Carrollton usually starts with an older wood fence on a lot built between the 1970s and the 1990s. The city sits north-northwest of Dallas and spreads across Dallas, Denton and Collin counties, and many of its subdivisions have alley-backed lots where the rear fence or gate faces the alley. This site is advertising for independent fence contractors and does not build or repair anything itself.

Call (214) 555-0137 and describe the job: a leaning fence, storm damage, a gate that will not open or a new fence. An independent contractor quotes the work, and the honest advice is to collect two or three comparable written quotes before you pick one. Carrollton has its own fence rules, so the sections below cover the City's permit trigger, height limits and what to ask before you sign.

services.title: Wood privacy fence installation
services.desc: A new cedar or pine privacy fence along an older Carrollton lot, including board-on-board styles. The contractor who quotes your job should show how the plan fits the City's 8-ft rear and side limit and your HOA's rules.

services.title: Fence repair and storm damage
services.desc: Leaning sections, rotted posts and missing pickets are common on 15 to 20 year old fences. Ask whether the repair stays under the 20 ft the City treats as the permit line.

services.title: Gate repair and automatic gates
services.desc: Sagging walk gates, failed latches and driveway openers that quit. Power wiring for an opener is electrical work, so ask the installer who holds the electrical licence.

services.title: Wrought iron and ornamental fences
services.desc: Tubular steel or aluminum fencing for a front yard or side run. The City limits a Carrollton front-yard fence to 36 inches and no more than 50 percent opacity, which suits open iron.

sections.heading: What the City of Carrollton says about fence permits
sections.html:
According to the City of Carrollton's building inspection page, a fence permit is required for any new fence over 20 ft in length, or when you relocate or repair more than 20 ft of an existing fence. A site plan showing the proposed fence location is required. The same page says replacing boards and posts up to 20 ft does not need a permit, and it prohibits fences in visibility easements and drainage easements.

The City's handout Fence Ordinance Outline for Customers (Ordinance 3563, effective August 2013) gives a maximum of 8 ft for both rear and side yards on single-family and duplex lots. Front-yard fences are limited to no greater than 36 inches with an opacity level not exceeding 50 percent. That handout is more than ten years old, so confirm the current rule with the City before you order materials.

Do not borrow numbers from another city. Dallas allows a higher maximum than Carrollton and uses a different permit trigger, so a Dallas article does not tell you what Carrollton will approve. Check with the City and your HOA before building; in many HOAs the association can still control fence type, so get written approval first. For the Dallas side of the picture, see fence installation in Dallas.

sections.heading: Older lots, alleys, clay and storm wind
sections.html:
A fence on a 1970s to 1990s Carrollton lot has usually been through a lot of North Texas weather. Much of the Dallas area sits on expansive clay that swells and shrinks with moisture, which is one reason posts shift and sections lean. The National Weather Service counts a thunderstorm with 58 mph winds as severe, so a fence that lasted two decades can still lose a section in one spring storm.

The repair-or-replace question usually comes down to how many posts have failed. One Dallas fence company advertises $25 to $60 per board installed, $300 to $800 for straightening a 10 to 30 ft leaning section, and $1,200 to $3,500 for a full panel rebuild after wind (20 to 50 ft). Because the City's permit line is 20 ft, a big repair may need a permit even though it is not a new fence. See fence repair for the wider picture.

On alley-backed lots, ask the contractor to check the plat or survey for easements before posts go in, because the City prohibits fences in visibility and drainage easements. Texas law requires you or your contractor to call 811 two business days before digging, and for a hired contractor the 811 call is the contractor's responsibility. Do not skip it because the yard is your own.

sections.heading: Pricing, gates and who to hire
sections.html:
Advertised prices vary widely, so read them as one firm's range and not as a quote. One DFW firm advertises $18 to $28 per linear foot installed for a standard 6 ft cedar privacy fence, while another advertises $30 to $60 for mid-range cedar at the same height. The first firm says board-on-board and shadow box styles typically add $2 to $5 per linear foot over a basic dog-ear fence. For iron, one DFW firm advertises $30 to $45 per linear foot for standard tubular steel; see fence costs and iron fences.

Gates are a separate line. One Dallas-area firm advertises that most residential automatic gate installations in the Dallas area run $3,500 to $10,000, and the same firm lists lower figures on another page, so treat any single number carefully. Opener power wiring is electrical work; ask the installer who holds the electrical licence. For a gate that has simply stopped working, start with gate repair.

Texas does not license fence contractors at the state level, and the City pages we read do not say whether Carrollton registers them. Ask the City, then ask each contractor for proof of insurance and a written scope that names the height, the materials and who pulls any permit. Neighboring Richardson, for example, requires fence contractors to be registered, so the rules differ city by city; see Richardson or Plano if your job is across the line.

faq.q: Do I need a permit for a fence in Carrollton?
faq.a: According to the City of Carrollton, a permit is required for any new fence over 20 ft in length, or when you relocate or repair more than 20 ft of an existing fence, and a site plan is required. Replacing boards and posts up to 20 ft does not need one. Confirm with the City and your HOA before work starts.

faq.q: How tall can a back fence be in Carrollton?
faq.a: The City's Fence Ordinance Outline for Customers (Ordinance 3563, effective 2013) gives a maximum of 8 ft for rear and side yards on single-family and duplex lots, and 36 inches with no more than 50 percent opacity in the front yard. The handout is old, so check the current rule with the City. Your HOA may set a lower limit or control the fence style.

faq.q: Does an alley-backed lot change what I can build?
faq.a: The City prohibits fences in visibility easements and drainage easements, and alley-backed lots often have utility or drainage strips near the rear line. This page cannot say what the City requires for an alley-side gate, so ask the City. Ask your contractor to check the plat or survey before posts go in, and make sure 811 is called.

faq.q: Who pays when a fence is shared with a neighbor?
faq.a: This is general information from TexasLawHelp, not legal advice. It says that if both neighbors use a fence straddling the boundary line, both own it and share the cost of repairing and replacing it, while a fence wholly on one lot belongs to that owner. Talk to your neighbor and get the boundary confirmed before you order work.
